Recent work supports learning retention within recurrence, but does not establish that this benchmark needs stronger forgetting. [Were RNNs All We Needed? (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01201) introduces minGRU: input-dependent coordinate-wise update gates, with hidden-state dependencies removed to enable parallel training. Useful evidence for selective recurrent retention, but its experiments do not demonstrate gains on these Amazon categories. [Parallelizable Memory Recurrent Units (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09495) explores persistent nonlinear memory with parallelizable computation; relevant context, rather than a replacement compatible with the required GRU4Rec backbone.

The closest practical alternative is to retain the standard GRU and diversify its existing update-gate timescales. [Tallec and Ollivier’s chrono initialization](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11188), an older foundational result, connects trainable gates to temporal scales and proposes gate-bias initialization for GRUs/LSTMs. Proposed adaptation: initialize coordinate-wise retention biases across short and longer horizons, then learn them jointly with the existing network. For h_t = z_t ⊙ h_{t−1} + (1−z_t) ⊙ candidate_t, constant retention z implies an approximate decay timescale −1/log(z). This describes the direct retention path, not the complete nonlinear model’s effective memory.

Compare this initialization against the corrected baseline and identity-gate control only after final-feature execution agrees across training, diagnostics and the embedded predictor. Preserve padding states and read the final nonpadding position. Treat improved memory allocation as a hypothesis, not evidence of excessive historical dependence; select using the fixed macro validation HR@10, with one jointly trained GRU model per category.
